evidence.text:
fix: de-conflict pavilion trinkets from the seat + align path stones
An adversarial layout review (Claude visual + measured rects ⨯ Codex 5.5 ⨯ a
4-agent geometry workflow) found the pavilion's token-trinkets were colliding
with the stool+cushion seat, and a courtyard prop was mis-layered:

- incense burner rendered ON the seat cushion at every pavilion tier (slot x42
  maps to interior-center where the bottom-anchored cushion sits).
- the hanging scroll dropped onto the cushion in the SHORT small/mid interiors
  — and the small tier shows ONLY the scroll, so it was the most-seen case.
  (Both Claude's and Codex's full-tier-only reasoning missed this; the workflow
  caught it using true sprite aspect ratios.)
- tea_set hit the stool at the mid tier; sleeping_cat sat on the stool at full.
- trinkets rendered as 7-17px dust at 1× — illegible.
- path_stones z=26 drew the "should recede" worn path IN FRONT of the
  pavilion/lantern/cairn, and y=95.4 sank it ~4pp below the ground line.

Fixes (config/markup only, no core change, no schema bump):
- Re-slotted all six trinkets so the interior-center seat stays clear: scroll
  high on the rear wall, wind_chime on the eave, tea_set+incense on the left
  floor, lucky_cat+sleeping_cat on the right. Verified collision-free vs
  stool/cushion and pairwise across small/mid/full and 1-6 unlocks, then
  re-measured in the live render (all overlaps now "none").
- Bumped trinket widths ~1.35× for legibility (a 2.5-3× bump was rejected as it
  re-introduced overlaps).
- path_stones z 26→12 (recede, per its own comment) and y 95.4→91.0 (align to
  the ground row).
- Reworded tea_set/incense i18n hints "table"→"floor" (no table sprite exists;
  a new asset was judged too expensive) and softened the trinket hover outline
  2px→1.5px + glow now that sprites are larger.

Courtyard ground row (bamboo/cherry/cat/willow/lantern/cairn/pavilion) was
reviewed and left as-is — its minor canopy-edge overlaps are natural and the
grass/rock-over-pavilion-base z-order is intentional foreground groundcover.

fix: re-layout pavilion interior per user feedback
Visual review surfaced four pavilion-interior issues:

1. Two cats in the pavilion (lucky_cat + sleeping_cat) plus the

   since its prone pose reads as a live pet, not a statue.
2. Cushion stacked on top of stool made the stool look like a stone
   table with a cushion sitting on it. Now placed BESIDE the stool on
   the floor — stool reads as the table, cushion reads as a floor
   seat, and the new table-top trinkets land cleanly.
3. tea_set + incense were on the floor at the far edges (16/72 and
   14/92). Moved both ONTO the stool top (38/62, 60/62) so the table
   metaphor lands.
4. scroll was already at the eave (50/12) — kept. wind_chime threshold
   dropped 100M → 50M to backfill the removed lucky_cat tier, and
   incense dropped 200M → 100M so the unlock curve still climbs
   monotonically.

Floor reads symmetric now: cushion (left) — stool/table (center) —
sleeping_cat (right). i18n hints updated to match new positions.

evidence.text:
fix: scrub last orphan pixel in front of west walk frame 1
User spotted one more speck the previous scrub missed: a cool-gray pixel
rgba(218,216,216) floating ~4 px in front of the cat's face in west walk
frame 1 (sheet x=80, y=94). The earlier cleanup only checked for cream
whites (R>=220 G>=200 B>=180) — this pixel was near-neutral gray with
R=218, just under the floor.

Generalized to a stricter scan: any near-neutral bright pixel (R>=200
with G,B within 30/40 of R) whose entire 8-neighborhood is transparent
is by definition an isolated stray and gets erased. A full-sheet pass
found exactly one such pixel — the one the user circled. The cat's own
white markings sit inside connected white regions, so the "isolated"
guard leaves them alone.
evidence.author: dipsy

evidence.text:
fix: scrub 2-pixel cluster artifact on west walk frame 3
User spotted yet another stray — but this one wasn't a single isolated
pixel, it was a 2-pixel vertical cluster at sheet (212, 94)-(212, 95),
floating just in front of west walk frame 3. Two reasons the previous
two scrub passes missed it:

  1. The two pixels are each other's neighbors, so the
     "all 8 neighbors transparent" guard rejected them as non-isolated.
  2. Their color was a dim neutral (153, 139, 141) — well below the
     R>=200 brightness threshold the earlier scrub used.

Generalized to the most principled detection: a connected-component
flood fill, treating any cluster with <=6 pixels as a stray (the cat
itself is one giant component per cell — 374-781 pixels each — so
small islands floating in the alpha-transparent sea are always
artifacts, regardless of color or shape). One pass found exactly the
2-pixel cluster the user circled and nothing else.

After-scrub verification: 26 connected components total (one per
non-empty cell), smallest is 374 px, largest 781 px — no orphans.
evidence.author: dipsy

evidence.text:
fix: scrub stray white pixels off cat walk frames
PixelLab's animation export left 1-10 stray cream-colored pixels
(#f2f0ee, #e7e2de) floating beyond the cat's body silhouette on EVERY
walk frame, just in front of the muzzle/nose. Probably anti-alias /
whisker residue. At 68px cells under desktop scaling they read as a
small white speck floating in front of the cat's face — the user
spotted it and circled it on the east strip.

Programmatically scrubbed via PIL: for each frame, found the body's
forward edge (rightmost orange pixel for east, leftmost for west), then
cleared any high-brightness pixels (R>=220 G>=200 B>=180, alpha>0) beyond
that edge to fully transparent. Row 0 (east): 16 px removed across 8
frames. Row 1 (west): 49 px (more verbose noise on that direction).
Row 2 (turn/idle): clean, untouched. Re-scan confirms 0 floating
whites beyond the body in every frame.

The cat's actual white markings (chin / chest / paws / belly) sit INSIDE
the body silhouette and are untouched — the orange-edge floodfill only
ever erases out-of-body pixels.

evidence.text:
fix(core): quarantine malformed rings memory instead of letting it die
The best-effort degrade added in 9ad9e5e kept summaries alive, but left a
malformed rings.json permanently poisonous: every load failed, nothing was
ever written again, and the only signal was an eprintln nobody sees in a
GUI app. High-water protection and ring history would silently stop
accumulating forever.

- malformed JSON is renamed to a dated rings.json.corrupt-* sibling and
  memory restarts from an empty book (the bad bytes are preserved, not
  destroyed)
- a schema_version newer than the reader still degrades WITHOUT touching
  the file: that is real history written by a newer binary, and a
  downgraded reader must not quarantine or overwrite it
- I/O errors keep propagating to the best-effort layer (may be transient)
- doc 11 records the PRD 2.0 I0 decision explicitly (display = high-water
  memory, accounting = live truth, retention alternative rejected) so the
  policy reads as a decision, not incidental architecture
evidence.author: dipsy

evidence.text:
fix(core): degrade garden memory failures
Treat rings.json as an auxiliary memory layer so corrupt or unwritable garden history cannot block cache hits or refreshes. Align CLI summary rendering with the desktop high-water display tiers, and route events.json through the same atomic temp-file write helper used by rings.

fix(web): name unpriced models in the cost tab; lazy-fetch; drop dead loadPrices
Review fixes on the cost core-ification merge:

- Medium: consuming only SummaryCost.total.by_model dropped the named
  unpriced-model rows the old panel showed (an unknown model moved only the
  aggregate "Unpriced" KPI, so the user could not tell WHICH model was

  unpriced_by_model (per-model tokens; sums back to unpriced_tokens), and the
  Cost tab renders a named row per unpriced model again — restoring the
  cost.rowUnknown / cost.unpriced strings the review flagged as newly dead.
- Low: the Cost tab fetched cost_estimate eagerly at drawer-mount (app
  startup, worst case a full first-run scan even if the tab is never opened);
  it now fetches lazily on activate() like the Insight tab, retrying there.
- Low: removed the dead JS loadPrices wrapper (no caller after the switch to
  loadCostEstimate); the load_prices/save_prices commands remain for a future
  price editor.

Verified: core 131 (incl. unpriced_by_model assertion) + cli 3 + tauri 8 +
web 60 green; browser-stubbed the cost_estimate shape and confirmed priced
rows (with echoed rates) and named unpriced rows both render, zero console
errors.

evidence.text:
fix(core): clamp Codex thread total to its rollout split
The SQLite thread total (canonical) and the rollout split come from two
stores that can disagree. If the DB total ever dipped below the split-bucket
sum, blended = total - split underflowed to 0 while the buckets were still
priced in full — attributing more tokens than the reported total. Clamp
total = max(db_total, split) so total >= input+output+cache always holds
(blended can't go negative, no bucket priced beyond the total). Adds a
regression test for the DB-undercount case; the normal DB-wins path (total
>= split) is unchanged.

evidence.text:
fix(web): repair cost-export tie sort + gate release tag version
Two follow-ups from review of the post-2.0 hardening branch:

- buildCostEstimateJson sorted its final tiebreaker on `project_key`, a
  field the export-privacy rename removed — two projects tied on
  usd/unpriced/display_name hit `undefined.localeCompare` → TypeError,
  failing the whole cost JSON export. Sort on the emitted `project_id`;
  added a tie-case regression test.
- release preflight now checks the v* tag equals the tauri-app crate and
  tauri.conf.json bundle version, so a `v2.0.1` tag can no longer publish
  `2.0.0` binaries.
evidence.author: dipsy

evidence.text:
fix(web): export privacy, formula injection, provider staleness + toast leak
Frontend half of the post-2.0 review fixes.

- data-export: the export intentionally omitted `project_path` for privacy, but
  `project_key` IS the on-disk path when known (core `event.project_key()` →
  `normalize_path(path)`), so the "pathless" CSV/JSON still baked `/Users/...`
  into a shareable file. Emit an opaque per-project id (FNV-1a of the key) plus
  the display name instead of the raw key; bump export JSON schema_version → 2.
- data-export: neutralize spreadsheet formula injection — a cell starting
  `= + - @` (e.g. a project dir named `=HYPERLINK(...)`) is prefixed with `'`
  so Excel/Sheets treat it as literal text.
- cost-panel / insight-panel: both cached the cost estimate for the whole
  session, so after the watcher delivered new work the figures went stale until
  restart. Recompute lazily when a new summary frame arrives (compared by
  identity, so reopening without new data still serves the cache).
- rings-panel: moved the rings.json disk read off mount onto first `activate()`
  — the drawer mounts all six providers eagerly at startup, so it was hitting
  disk on every launch even when the drawer was never opened.
- error-toast: `pruneStack` removed a toast's DOM node but left its `recent`
  entry (and timer) behind, so the next same-source error collapsed onto a
  detached node — invisible, timer never firing. Clean the entry like dismiss().

Rewrites the data-export tests to the id-based shape and adds assertions that no
raw path leaks and that formula injection is neutralized (web suite 79 → 81).

unclassified.text:
fix: clear flowerbed flowers on re-render (stacking/leak)
Second missed piece from the flowerbed promotion. render-flowerbed.js
appends `.pg6-flower` elements without self-clearing, relying on
clearDynamicLayers() to remove the previous render's flowers. main's
dynamicLayerSelector didn't list `.pg6-flower` / `.pg6-flower-tooltip`,
so each watcher tick re-appended 366 flowers on top of the old set —
unbounded stacking + DOM leak. Only shows on desktop after a scan tick;
the static browser preview never re-renders so it looked fine.

Added both selectors. Deliberately did NOT copy the D branch's list
verbatim — D had `.pg6-garden-cat` in it, but main intentionally keeps
the cat out of the clear list (its long-lived rAF wander loop must
survive re-renders).

unclassified.text:
fix(web): close the drawer-content review findings
Fixes from the max-effort review of 95e7330 (14 findings + 4 sweep
addenda; the demo-sample privacy rebuild landed separately in 40fd58a):

- demo gate: loadRings/loadPrices return null under ?demo=1, so a
  desktop demo session can never render real garden memory or the
  user's prices.json next to the canned scene
- drawer update() forwards ticks only to the visible tab; hidden tabs
  stash the latest frame and catch up via the new activate() hook when
  selected - this also retires five hidden re-renders per watcher tick
- rings-panel caches its book: update() re-renders memory, activate()
  re-reads the backend; a loaded book never blanks to the loading
  placeholder (the per-tick IPC storm and skeleton flicker are gone)
- cost-panel retries a failed price load on activation instead of
  showing "unavailable" for the rest of the session
- formatUsd pins 'en' grouping (matching the repo's other formatters):
  browser-default locales rendered $1,235 as "$1.235"
- rings journal per PRD P1-3: localized dates and month group headers
  (app locale, UTC-pinned), a garden-age summary line, tier rows reuse
  the unlock-banner copy instead of raw entity/to tokens, sentinel
  subtitles dropped for the first-seen project path, and the two
  PRD-defined future event types are pre-titled
- composition sources render friendly adapter names via the shared
  sourceLabel helper (was raw 'claude-code' / 'manual-jsonl')
- kpiCard/closeButton hoisted to render-helpers (three copies each
  before); dead savePrices shim removed; the impossible event_type
  fallback and its fixture test replaced with real-shape tests that
  compare against t() instead of hardcoding copy; stale garden_rings

unclassified.text:
fix: harden flowerbed after adversarial review (bundle bloat, a11y, view sync)
A 4-dimension review (rust / frontend / hygiene / schema) with per-finding
skeptic verification surfaced 10 real issues out of 14 (4 rejected as false
alarms — e.g. "level isn't self-relative" was wrong, the manifest checked
out). Fixes the confirmed ones:

build.rs (MEDIUM — shipped bloat):
- The asset mirror copied a 1.4 MB image-gen source PNG
  (flowerbed_source_imagegen.png), the unused master sheet (flowers.png),
  and the _brief/ authoring notes into every user's Tauri bundle. copy_dir
  now skips `_source*` files, `flowers.png`, and any `_`-prefixed sprite
  subdir. Verified: web/assets/sprites/flowerbed/ now mirrors only the 20
  runtime flower_l*_*.png.

web/index.html (a11y):
- Flowers ignored OS prefers-reduced-motion under the default motion=system.
  Added .pg6-flower / .pg6-flower-tooltip to the global reduced-motion query.

web/render-flowerbed.js (a11y):
- 366 flowers were each tabIndex=0 → hundreds of keyboard tab stops. Flowers
  are now non-focusable (overview view; data is keyboard-reachable via the
  Dashboard heatmap). Hover/focus tooltip listeners kept for a future roving
  pattern.

web/garden.js (view consistency):
- With auto_rescan off, the mini-heatmap / dashboard / insight refreshed on
  watcher ticks while the cached scene did not, so the year-views diverged.
  All views now pause together; returnDiff still records the true latest.

docs (stale references):
- CLAUDE.md + cherry-petal spec said schema v4; actual is v6. Corrected both.
- Tightened the flowerbed_level docstring: it shares the log-ratio formula
  with size_level but uses a different baseline (log10(2) vs 3.0) and band
  count (4 vs 5) — they're tuned independently.

Not changed (reviewed, judged out of scope): the URL ?flowerbed= override
shadowing the settings radio only affects the browser-preview PoC path
(desktop has no query string); the committed garden-summary.json fixture is
existing practice; the UTC-vs-local fallback keying was rejected as not a
real divergence.

unclassified.text:
fix: carry flowerbed through settings normalization
The flowerbed promotion missed web/data-source.js. Its normalizeSettings()
is a whitelist — any field not explicitly listed is stripped when settings
round-trip through the Tauri get_settings/set_settings path. flowerbed
wasn't in the whitelist, so on desktop:

  get_settings → normalizeSettings drops appearance.flowerbed
  → shouldRenderFlowerbed() reads undefined → always false
  → flowers never render, even with the Settings toggle on.

Browser preview hid the bug because ?flowerbed=enabled overrides the
setting before normalization matters.

Added flowerbed to both defaultSettings() and the normalizeSettings()
validChoice whitelist, matching the D PoC branch's data-source.js change
that didn't get ported in the promotion commit.

fix: buffer atomic event cache writes
Large event caches were serialized directly into File, turning serde's small writes into sustained syscall-heavy refreshes. Buffer JSON output while preserving the existing private temp file and atomic rename semantics.

unclassified.text:
fix: seal the state-semantics edges from the batch review
Five findings from the owner's review of the v1.4 watch-mode batch —
two Medium state-boundary bugs and three Low polish items:

- demo mode no longer mounts unlock moments: diffing the canned garden
  against the user's real seen-frame fired fake banners and then wrote
  demo tiers into pg6.seen.tiers, poisoning the next live session
- garden.js splits visibleSummary from latestSummary: the watcher only
  advances the latest ledger while auto_rescan is off, so a settings
  tweak or renderer switch repaints the frame the user was actually
  shown instead of leaking paused data; flipping auto_rescan back on
  folds latest into visible and feeds the unlock pipeline that frame
- a banner wiped by a full scene repaint no longer holds the queue
  hostage for its dwell timer: a childList observer hands the slot to
  the next entry immediately (a repaint storm may fast-forward through
  queued banners - deliberate trade against frozen slots)
- rings quarantine names bump a numeric suffix when the same second
  already produced one (Windows rename-onto-existing fails, which would
  have demoted quarantine back to permanent degrade); regression test
- the tray's "No token activity yet" empty row joins tr(en, zh)

unclassified.text:
fix(web): re-load the rings book on each share-card activation
The share drawer mounts the weekly + year providers once at startup, so
ensureRings() — which set ringsLoaded and never cleared it — cached the
book for the whole app lifetime. A ring moment recorded after the first
open never reached a later card (open drawer → keep working → reopen shows
stale moments). activate() now invalidates the cache so each open re-reads;
within one activation the fetch is still shared by preview + export, so the
"once per activation" comment is now true. Mirrors the Cost/Projects tabs'
invalidate-on-activate freshness (post-2.0 review).

Adds a provider-level regression test that mounts the weekly provider with
a loadRings spy and asserts a re-load on the second activation.

doctor (v1.7):
- the state-dir "not writable" arm now redacts the home path like every
  other check (was forwarding ensure_writable_dir's raw display() string) —
  doctor --json is meant to be paste-safe per the README
- an absent state dir reports Warn instead of create_dir_all-ing it, so the
  read-mostly diagnostic no longer materializes ~/.local-agent-garden/ on a
  never-launched machine; the write probe cleans up on all failure paths
- load failures are classified: parse error -> Error ("invalid"), IO/
  permission error -> Warn ("unreadable"), so a valid-but-locked file no
  longer fails the run with corruption wording
- run() derives state paths from ctx's home (not process env) so a
  with_home(X) caller gets a coherent report; redaction is now a pure,
  env-free, boundary-aware helper (no /Users/su -> ~perproj over-redaction)
  with an injected-fixture test

year/weekly cards (v1.8):
- year card's closing line flows below the actual project rows, fixing the
  >=5-project overlap (the 3-row weekly Y-rhythm was inherited); the
  zero-token card prints the quiet-year line once, not twice
- shared date/stat helpers hoisted into card-canvas.js (were byte-identical
  copies in both cards); year title uses the shared PAPER constant; both
  cards focus the export button after the preview renders, not while it is
  synchronously disabled (was dropping focus to <body>)

shared:
- fmtLocal rolls a rounds-to-1000 value into the next unit (999,950,000 ->
  1.0B, not 1000.0M); year-card test is timezone-independent via an injected
  calendar-day anchor

Deferred (architecture, tracked): moving doctor's English message/detail
prose out of core and the adapter-inventory shape into core — both serve the
not-yet-built Tauri health UI and would churn the just-shipped doctor --json
support shape, so they belong with that consumer.

unclassified.text:
fix: sweep the remaining review findings
Closes the six open findings from the feat/prd-2.0 branch review (one
deliberately declined, see below).

- version skew: unknown tier strings in the rings snapshot (e.g. written
  by a newer binary) are preserved by the high-water merge instead of
  silently ranking 0 and demoting the garden; transitions the current
  binary cannot order never emit a tier_up event. rank() now returns
  Option to make the unknown case impossible to ignore
- tray midnight rollover: a timer re-reads the cache just after each UTC
  midnight, so the "today" glance line stops asserting yesterday on
  quiet days (the menu otherwise only rebuilds on garden:updated)
- one home for the UTC day-key contract: aggregate::utc_day_key /
  day_key replace seven hand-typed "%Y-%m-%d" sites across daily maps,
  rings, tray and CLI — the exact format the timezone regression class
  needs to stay greppable
- normalizeCoreTiers drops its dead camelCase tolerance: core locks
  snake_case, so a wire-shape change must fail loudly, not half-work
- web/data/garden-summary.json regenerated at schema 7 with a tiers
  block (now pinned to the sample's own last_seen so the demo lantern
  reads lit); the browser demo exercises the core-tiers path while the
  JS fallback keeps covering pre-tiers summaries — verified byte-equal
- half-wired rings plumbing (loadRings / garden_rings) carries
  TODO(prd-2.0 §6.1 I7) markers pointing at the data-drawer rings tab

Declined: caching the tray's per-event settings reads — an invalidating
cache adds coupling for negligible TOML I/O (YAGNI).

unclassified.text:
fix(core): correctness + privacy hardening from post-2.0 review
Two independent review passes converged on a set of core-side defects that
per-feature reviews missed. None change on-disk shapes, so no schema bump.

- aggregate: `size_strength` computed 0/0 = NaN when the busiest project sat
  exactly on the 10k-token floor (max_tokens == 9999). serde renders NaN as
  `null`, which the tray's `GardenSummary` re-parse rejects — silently freezing
  the tray menu. Fill the removable singularity (top project → 1.0) instead.
- codex: `extract_token_total` summed `total_tokens` together with the
  input/output/cache components it already accounts for, ~2x-inflating every
  Codex row's tokens (and thus cost/stage/heatmap). Prefer an explicit total;
  only sum components when none is present. The old test enshrined the bug.
- codex: `discover()` only checked the SQLite db / session index, so a
  rollout-only install (`sessions/`) was skipped entirely — `scan` gates
  `collect()` on `discover()`. Recognize the rollout dirs `collect()` reads.
- codex: open the threads DB by path, not a `file:` URI, which malformed and
  dropped the whole source when the home path contained `#` / `?` / `%`.
- cache: a cache hit ignored `sources_filter` (returned the full set), and a
  filtered scan persisted its subset into the shared `events.json` — then served
  whole to later unfiltered reads. Filter on hit; only persist a full scan.
- prices: reject negative / non-finite user rates instead of emitting negative
  or `null` (NaN) cost.

Adds fixture tests for each (size_strength floor, codex sessions-only discover
+ prefer-total, cache source-filter, negative-rate rejection).

unclassified.text:
ci+docs: gate releases behind a preflight job; correct schema-version note

fix: align today-key timezone and consolidate tier logic after review
The 07-06 review found the flat renderer (and the new garden-tiers.js)
looking up daily_activity with local-date keys while aggregate.rs emits
UTC day keys - between local and UTC midnight the WALL view zeroed
todayActivity and unlit the lantern while the 2.5D view stayed lit.

- unlockTier now lives only in web/garden-tiers.js (UTC day keys); both

unclassified.text:
fix: de-paper-flip the wandering cat's turn-around
The garden cat used `scaleX(1) → scaleX(-1)` interpolated linearly over
4% of the wander keyframe, which meant scaleX passed through ~0 for a
couple of frames — the cat visibly collapsed to a vertical line on each
turn (the "paper cat" report). The 360° rotate that accompanied it also
read as a gymnastic spin, off-character for a cat.

New turn choreography (still in a single keyframe, no DOM changes):
  50%   walk arrives at the right edge
  53%   crouch: scaleY 0.88 (anticipation)
  56%   peak hop: translateY −10, scaleY 1.10 (stretch)
  56.01% facing flips IN MID-AIR: scaleX(1) → scaleX(-1)
         (near-zero-time step ≈ 1.5ms — no interpolated zero-width frame)
  60%   land: scaleY back to 1.0, walking back
The scaleY squash/stretch hides the instant scaleX flip behind a
visible body motion, so the eye reads "the cat hopped and turned"
instead of "the cat became a line." The 360° rotate is gone.
unclassified.author: dipsy

unclassified.text:
fix: motion=off no longer blanks the whole garden
The data-motion="off" CSS rule applied `display: none !important` to
`.pg6-sprite` and `.pg6-info`, not just the season particles. So a user
who set motion to "off" (an accessibility/preference choice) lost every
project vine, courtyard object, and the hover info card — the entire
garden vanished, leaving only the static wall + sky.

motion=off now kills animation/transition on sprites and the info card
(keeping them visible) and removes only `.pg6-season-particle`, which is
pure ambient motion. Found via an adversarial review pass; the over-broad
selector was introduced alongside the season-particle work.
unclassified.author: dipsy

unclassified.text:
fix: box large TOML errors for clippy
Windows CI on Rust 1.85 denies clippy::result_large_err, and the TOML parse variant made the crate Error enum large enough for every Result<_, Error> to fail. Keep the public typed Error enum but box the TOML source errors so the Err variant stays small across platforms.

unclassified.text:
test: lock the UTC today-key contract with a node regression test
The c99b4ff timezone fix had no guard: nothing stopped a future edit
from reverting unlockTier's today lookup to local-date keys, silently
re-splitting the WALL and 2.5D views around midnight for non-UTC users.

- unlockTier takes an injectable `now` (house style from CLAUDE.md:
  parameterize time instead of mocking Date); callers are unchanged
- web/tests/garden-tiers.test.mjs asserts UTC-key hits and local-key
  misses at a fixed diverging instant, deterministic in any machine tz
- new `web-tests` CI job runs `node --test` on runner-preinstalled
  Node (the glob form: the directory form misfires on Node 24)
- web/package.json only marks web/ as ESM for Node; the frontend still

- previousIsoWeek now anchors on the user's LOCAL calendar day (injectable

  The pure-UTC anchor served a UTC+8 user the week BEFORE last between

- the share drawer's menu rows reused the pg6-share-row/-name class names
  the composition tab's share bars already owned, so the drawer's paper

  Renamed the drawer side to pg6-share-item*.
